title: Understand the Anchor Audit

source.manuscript_title: Auditing allele rankings in genomic predictions: consequence controls and contact-map anchoring
source.scope: Source-linked educational adaptation of an unsubmitted research manuscript. Human author approval and learner validation are not certified by this toolkit.
source.publication_status: Unsubmitted review candidate; no journal acceptance or new DOI claimed.

lessons.title: Start with the right object
lessons.summary: A map, a diagram and a score answer different questions.
body: A contact map has a value for each pair of genomic bins. A persistence diagram summarizes when graph features appear and disappear as an edge threshold changes. A single aggregate score is a further summary; it cannot recover the map.

The study used predicted log-enrichment maps. These signed values are not observed read counts. The toolkit starts later in the workflow: you supply finite diagram coordinates and a declared shift. It does not request predictions or compute persistence from a contact matrix.
Keep reference and alternate bins, masks, track and filtration conventions aligned before creating diagrams. Changing that support changes the scientific comparison.
lessons.try_it: List which information a diagram preserves and which genomic locations it can discard.
lessons.boundary: An abstract degree-one feature is not automatically a located chromatin loop.

lessons.title: A stable distance can still change a rank
lessons.summary: Small score changes and large ranking changes can coexist.
body: Bottleneck distance matches diagram points while allowing points to be matched to the diagonal. The cost is the largest displacement in the best matching. A point can disappear at a cost equal to half its lifetime.

On the same finite support, a bound on every edge-value change bounds the resulting diagram distance. This is a standard stability result. It does not require treating an arbitrary contact transform as a metric.
Ranks answer a different question. If two scores are tied, even a small difference can select a unique leader. A stable numerical score therefore does not guarantee a stable rank.
lessons.try_it: Two scores are both 1.000. One becomes 1.001. Has the score changed much? Has the unique-leader decision changed?
lessons.boundary: Mathematical stability does not establish biological calibration.

lessons.title: Move the origin, preserve interval lengths
lessons.summary: Centering translates both coordinates of each interval.
body: For the study filtration, subtracting a map-wide mean adds that mean to every interval birth and death. The lifetime, death minus birth, stays fixed. The two maps can shift by different amounts.

Let delta be the alternate mean minus the reference mean. The audit computes the distance between the reference diagram and the alternate diagram shifted by lambda times delta. Lambda runs from zero to one. It is a preprocessing path, not a sequence or biological trajectory.

The distance can change by at most the absolute shift. Endpoint bounds enclose the intervening path. Exact equality at that bound forces a straight path; a small floating-point residual alone does not prove exact equality.
lessons.try_it: Use reference (0,4), alternate (1,5), and shift 0.25. Check that the lifetime stays 4 while distance rises from 1 to 1.25.
lessons.boundary: Numerical near-saturation is not a formal certificate for unseen higher-precision model outputs.

lessons.title: Leave uncertain winners unresolved
lessons.summary: A tolerance and score bounds make the ranking rule explicit.
body: The top set contains every score within the chosen tolerance of the maximum. When the selected allele belongs to a tie, fractional credit divides one by the size of that top set. Ties are not silently broken by array order.

Bounds can identify possible winners, guaranteed members of the top set, and guaranteed unique leaders. A sufficient native-margin bound can protect a strict leader throughout the path. When a bound is inconclusive, the right output is an unresolved set.

A Hausdorff witness is a lower bound obtained from nearest-point or diagonal distances. It can strengthen a decision without another full matching. It can miss multiplicity constraints, so it is not a replacement for bottleneck distance.
lessons.try_it: Increase the tie tolerance in the lab. Explain why a previously unique leader can become unresolved without changing any diagram.
lessons.boundary: A unique maximum is not evidence that the selected allele is clinically correct.

lessons.title: Interpret the earlier AVI result precisely
lessons.summary: A significant conditional result can have a negative observed margin.
body: The historical AVI counts rank Euclidean distances from a background centroid. They are not established rankings of raw AVI values. This distinction matters in a paper about anchor-sensitive rankings.

The mean statistic is the selected distance minus the larger competing distance. In the reported missense analysis the observed average was negative, but the simulated matched-null average was more negative. The significant result therefore describes enrichment relative to that null, not average superiority to the strongest alternative.

Some reported small adjusted values came from zero exceedances in a finite simulation. They are estimates at the simulation resolution floor. The frozen significant-count criterion and its remaining Monte Carlo uncertainty are both retained.
lessons.try_it: An observed margin is -0.01 and a simulated-null mean is -0.08. State one conclusion the difference supports and one it does not.
lessons.boundary: Neither background-distance ranking nor null-relative enrichment supplies an independently validated pathogenic-versus-benign classifier.

lessons.title: Separate exact arithmetic from a scientific null
lessons.summary: The calculation can be exact while the model remains conditional.
body: At each site, the study compared all three non-reference substitutions. Selected-allele credit records whether the clinically selected substitution is among the top scores, with ties sharing credit.

The label tests held the computed maps fixed and used specified probabilities for which allele would be selected. Exact finite-label arithmetic computes that conditional distribution without Monte Carlo sampling error. It does not make the selection process a randomized clinical experiment.

No discovery primary or sensitivity test survived Holm adjustment across the sixteen-test family. This did not establish the absence of every biological effect. Different representations and label models answer different questions.
lessons.try_it: Explain why exact probability arithmetic cannot prove that clinically selected alleles were exchangeable.
lessons.boundary: Null reference intervals are not biological effect confidence intervals.

lessons.title: Find the mechanism before celebrating the ranking
lessons.summary: Centering resolved many native ties without replacing strict leaders.
body: The discovery audit found numerical endpoint saturation across its computed allele comparisons. Some distances increased and others decreased. The sign of the response depended on relative diagram location.

Centering resolved 72 native ties while preserving all 45 strict native leaders. The observed path mechanism concerns how preprocessing changes the comparison. It does not by itself establish a useful gain in clinical discrimination.

Adding the absolute mean shift to the native distance reconstructed many centered top sets, but not all. Two diagrams can share the same native distance and shift while responding in opposite directions.
lessons.try_it: Compare alternates (1,5) and (-1,3) against reference (0,4), with the same positive shift. Why does the scalar native distance not tell you the direction?
lessons.boundary: Local saturation is ordinary on a nonflat piece of a finite matching problem; its frequency is not a new generic theorem.

lessons.title: Ask what actually replicated
lessons.summary: More unique ranks did not produce a consistent clinical-credit gain.
body: The new spatial cohort and protocol were fixed before those maps were acquired. It contained 84 sites in seven other loci. New spatial outcomes were prospective; independence from model training was not established.

All 66 native ties became unique maxima, and all 18 strict native leaders were preserved. Yet selected-allele credit fell descriptively from about 0.359 to 0.321. The sharper ranks and the selected-label outcome therefore moved in different directions.

The stronger witness bounds identified additional endpoint leaders beyond the simple margin check. This measures decision yield. A runtime speedup was not benchmarked, and no new confirmatory clinical-enrichment test was added.
lessons.try_it: Give a one-sentence conclusion that includes both tie resolution and the credit decrease.
lessons.boundary: Eighty-four overlapping windows do not represent 84 independent genomic regions.

lessons.title: Match the conclusion to numerical resolution
lessons.summary: Tolerance, delivered precision and solver error have distinct roles.
body: The delivered map values lie on a finite precision grid. This makes resolution relevant to ties, but does not isolate quantization as the cause of every tie or saturation event. Higher-precision source predictions would be needed for that comparison.

A tie tolerance defines an analysis convention. A numerical allowance is a claimed budget for computation error. Neither automatically becomes a physical detection limit. If coordinate units change, both must be scaled with the scores.

The paper reports numerical witnesses using practical allowances. It does not provide a complete interval-arithmetic certificate for every solver operation. The software likewise distinguishes numerical checks from formal real-arithmetic proof.
lessons.try_it: Multiply all diagram coordinates and shifts by ten. What else must be multiplied by ten to preserve the same ranking rule?
lessons.boundary: Reproducing floating-point outputs does not reveal the model’s unexposed internal precision.

lessons.title: Use reproducibility to answer the right question
lessons.summary: A rerun supports computation; independent measurements support biology.
body: The validation reran cached-input calculations and checked source-specific numerical claims. Replaying original random seeds can reproduce a simulation exactly without reducing its statistical uncertainty.

This toolkit adds reusable software and teaching examples. Its presets are synthetic. Imported diagrams are supplied by the user and processed locally by the static browser application. The study-summary panel contains aggregate author analysis results, not raw contact maps.

The research contribution combines a specified preprocessing path, ranking bounds, useful witnesses, explicit unresolved cases and measured new-locus behavior. It is not a new generic distance, a physical loop detector or a clinical prediction tool.
lessons.try_it: Describe one independent measurement that would be needed to connect the audit to a real structural chromosome change.
lessons.boundary: The practice quiz has not been validated with human learners and does not replace author review.

quiz.prompt: What input does this toolkit directly audit?
choices: Finite persistence diagrams plus a declared shift
Raw sequencing reads
A list of pathogenicity labels
quiz.explanation: The toolkit starts from diagram coordinates. Map acquisition and persistent-homology construction are upstream steps.

quiz.prompt: What stays unchanged when both coordinates of each interval receive the same shift?
choices: Every distance between two independently shifted diagrams
Each interval’s lifetime
Every allele ranking
quiz.explanation: Death minus birth is unchanged. Different shifts of the two diagrams can still change their distance and the resulting ranks.

quiz.prompt: For a valid 1-Lipschitz anchor path, what does exact endpoint saturation imply?
choices: The selected allele is pathogenic
The same matching remains optimal everywhere
The path is affine on that segment
quiz.explanation: The endpoint envelopes coincide. This conclusion does not require a fixed matching or extend beyond the segment.

quiz.prompt: Which statement describes the reported replication?
choices: More ties resolved, while selected-allele credit decreased descriptively
Every clinical metric improved
An experimental loop perturbation was validated
quiz.explanation: Tie resolution and selected-label credit are different outcomes. More unique ranks did not establish improved clinical discrimination.

quiz.prompt: A floating-point saturation residual is very small. What has been established?
choices: Exact equality for unseen real-valued model outputs
Numerical near-saturation on the computed inputs
The biological model has no error
quiz.explanation: A tiny computed residual is numerical evidence. A formal enclosure needs justified error bounds for every relevant operation.

quiz.prompt: What does an exact conditional label test guarantee?
choices: The clinically selected labels are exchangeable
Overlapping windows are biologically independent
The specified finite-label probabilities were computed without simulation error
quiz.explanation: Exact arithmetic addresses the calculation, not the truth of the label model or biological independence.

quiz.prompt: A mean margin is negative but exceeds its conditional-null mean. A significant test supports which reading?
choices: Enrichment relative to that null
A positive average lead over the strongest alternative
Validated clinical accuracy
quiz.explanation: A statistic can be negative yet unusually large under a more-negative null. The observed and null-relative effects must both be reported.

quiz.prompt: Does this model-output audit establish physical chromatin remodeling?
choices: Yes, whenever the diagram distance changes
No, independent structural evidence is still needed
Yes, if all ties disappear
quiz.explanation: Predicted maps and abstract intervals are not direct experimental evidence of a located chromosome change.

quiz.prompt: All coordinates and shifts are multiplied by ten. How should a fixed-unit ranking rule be transported?
choices: Keep the tolerance unchanged
Divide the tolerance by ten
Multiply the tolerance and numerical allowance by ten
quiz.explanation: Distances scale with the coordinate unit. Co-scaling thresholds preserves the intended comparisons.

quiz.prompt: A finite simulation produces zero exceedances. What should be reported?
choices: The plus-one estimate, draw count and Monte Carlo uncertainty
A true tail probability of exactly zero
An adjusted-value standard error obtained by rescaling a raw-p error
quiz.explanation: Finite simulation has a resolution floor. Raw-p uncertainty cannot simply be relabeled as adjusted-q uncertainty.

quiz.prompt: A new analysis deletes genomic bins. Can the same-support stability statement be used unchanged?
choices: Yes, because all topological summaries ignore support
No, deletion changes the object and needs its own analysis
Yes, provided the diagrams have the same number of points
quiz.explanation: The theorem requires common support. Equal point counts do not restore deleted bins or the original filtration.

quiz.prompt: Two cases share a native distance and shift, but their distances move in opposite directions. What fails?
choices: The definition of lifetime
The possibility of diagram matching
Universal reconstruction from those two scalar summaries alone
quiz.explanation: Relative diagram location contains directional information absent from the native scalar score and shift.

glossary.definition: The map-wide scalar used to set the origin of the diagram coordinates.
A non-reference DNA base at the same genomic position.
The smallest possible largest matching cost between two diagrams, allowing diagonal matches.
Thresholds at which a persistent feature appears and disappears.
Subtracting a declared map-wide mean from a map.
A specified model for labels while the observed maps and analysis choices are held fixed.
Matching an interval to birth = death at a cost of half its lifetime.
Credit of one divided by the tied top-set size when the selected allele belongs to that set; otherwise zero.
A nearest-point-or-diagonal lower bound on the bottleneck distance; it does not enforce matching multiplicities.
Death minus birth for one persistence interval.
Uncertainty introduced by estimating a probability or expectation using a finite number of random draws.
A collection, with multiplicity, of feature birth/death coordinate pairs.
An endpoint change that attains its mathematical Lipschitz bound exactly; numerical near-saturation is a separate empirical statement.
The clinically selected allele in the research design, not an independently proven correct prediction for each test.
The score gap that the analysis treats as unresolved.
Alternatives whose supplied score bounds do not yet justify a single winner.

nonclaims: Synthetic presets are teaching examples, not genomic observations.
The toolkit does not infer pathogenicity or locate chromatin loops.
Numerical near-saturation is not formal real-arithmetic certification.
Aggregate study results concern predicted maps on one selected track and overlapping loci.
The interactive quiz is practice with answer feedback, not a validated human transfer assessment.
assessment_scope: These multiple-choice practice items adapt the source reading guide. They are not the locked free-response human transfer test used in the manuscript validation harness. No learner pass rate or educational effectiveness is claimed.
